Candy Squares

Game StrategyParity

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Eat one heap and split the other into two. The player who cannot split loses.
How to play: Press between two squares in a heap to cut it. The other heap vanishes.

Look for the math

Only the heap you cut matters — the other is eaten. The winning secret is parity: even versus odd lengths.

Even means you can win

If at least one heap has even length, you have a winning plan: cut that even heap into two odd pieces. Your opponent then faces two odd heaps. The logic test checks every pair of lengths up to 20: from any position with an even heap there is a cut to both-odd, and from both-odd every cut leaves an even.

Odd plus odd always leaves an even

Splitting an odd number always produces one even piece and one odd piece (odd = even + odd). So after you face two odds, whatever you do hands the opponent an even heap — and they can answer back to two odds again.

The end is (1, 1)

Ones cannot be split. Perfect play from both-odd ends with you staring at (1, 1). The test checks that “both odd” matches the true loser-to-move for every pair of heaps up to 12 under perfect replies.

Deal a position with an even heap and always cut it into two odds. Watch the computer’s answers — they should keep leaving you an even heap until you can finish.
